items.title: No validated booking-time model
items.whyItMatters: Published models are mostly at high risk of bias and rarely validated (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Develop with pre-specified predictors and penalisation, and validate on a later period.

items.title: Measuring nausea and mobilisation
items.whyItMatters: Charts miss nausea severity and mobilisation times (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Use rescue antiemetic doses as a validated proxy (claim c5) or collect data prospectively.

items.title: List position is both a predictor and a decision
items.whyItMatters: List order is partly chosen by risk, so its association with failure mixes cause and selection.
items.opportunity: Model list position explicitly and report predictions for early and late positions.

items.title: Patients living alone or far away
items.whyItMatters: They worry most about same-day discharge and may be converted late.
items.opportunity: Include living arrangement and travel distance as candidate predictors and report calibration for these groups.

items.title: Surgeon effects
items.whyItMatters: Surgeons cluster; ignoring it overstates precision.
items.opportunity: Account for surgeon clustering and avoid ranking surgeons.

errorsFound: The need counts 'a drain' as a patient predictor; drain placement is a surgeon decision made during the operation and is not available at booking.
reevaluation: The gaps point to a model built with attention to events per predictor, measurement of nausea and list position, and validation.
summary: Five gaps; validation and measurement are high severity.
